install_semantics.signature: OwnedWorldBackend.install(prepared: PreparedWorldBackend, *, lineage: RNGOperation | None) -> None
facts: Enters native install scope with required explicit lineage; authentic None is standalone, otherwise forward genuine active ancestor operation.
Validates handle membership/revision/current token before any install assignment; requires prepared private RNG.
Publishes state.backend and state.rng by direct tuple assignment at W1129, clears local failure, increments owner revision, deletes handle from issuer registry, consumes current token.
Backend is replaced by the final prepared object; no guarantee preserves prior provider, Parameter, gradient or tensor-storage identities.
No user callback, serializer or public observation hook occurs inside this install body.
Core admission/completion still applies around the body; assignment success does not waive later completion failure policy.

install_semantics.signature: SharedWorldBackend.install(prepared: PreparedWorldBackend, *, lineage: RNGOperation | None) -> None
facts: Enters native install scope; an already-installed bootstrap has an earlier explicit refusal at W1340-1341.
Validates handle, rejects private RNG ownership, and stages any prepared ambient continuation before first backend assignment.
Publishes state.backend at W1352, updates bootstrap state when building, clears local failure, increments revision, deletes handle and consumes token.
No user installation callback or public identity observer; replaces prior backend with the final retained candidate.

For ordinary ready shared owner, consumed-handle membership refusal is reached before ambient staging and backend assignment. During the special bootstrap installed state, the earlier bootstrap guard is a different refusal and must not be mislabeled consumed-handle evidence.

Direct native RND installation is different from managed owner installation: retains the receiving RND Python object's identity, marks the authentic prepared record consumed, and replaces self.__dict__ with prepared.attributes.
Prepared modules/optimizer/pending rows replace prior attributes; pre-prepare Parameter, gradient and storage identities are not promised preserved.
_PreparedRND is an implementation-specific native record, not the opaque managed PreparedWorldBackend nor a public managed-owner custody/identity witness.
Direct RND behavior does not authorize bypassing managed owner wrappers to inspect or mutate their live provider.
PreparedWorldBackend is an opaque nonconstructible/nonportable/nondeepcopyable identity; all candidate objects remain issuer-retained.
Private restore clones factory output, runs validator and native load on that candidate, then clones the candidate again at W1091 before issuance.
Private learning reset invokes prepare_native then clones candidate at W1120 before issuance.
Shared restore clones candidate after validation/load at W1307; shared learning reset clones after prepare_native at W1335.
Consequently an identity baseline collected from a factory, validator or prepare_native callback is not the final installed candidate identity under ordinary deepcopy semantics.
Known checkpoint bytes and independently built expected providers establish value expectations, not installed object/Parameter/gradient/storage identity.
Arbitrary custom deepcopy behavior is outside the ordinary source profile and is not a supported identity-preservation workaround.

recipe: Use the same authentic owner and exact genuine handle for prepare, first install, and immediate second install.
Forward the actual current lineage for each call; perform no snapshot/capture/call or other observation between first install and retry.

On ordinary private or ready shared owner, the first install deletes the handle. The second fails the exact-type/retained-membership test W941-942 before destination-revision comparison W944, current-token validation W946, shared ambient checks/staging, or backend/RNG assignment.
Assert the actual consumed/foreign/fabricated membership refusal text and causal ordering; do not replace the handle or manufacture registry state.

Perform any managed observation only after the immediate retry if preserving that ordering; this observes post-refusal state, but does not independently create a missing pre-refusal identity baseline.
consumed_retry.source_proven_nonmutation: The ordinary consumed-refusal body reaches no provider, Parameter, gradient, storage, RNG-publication, owner revision, handle-deletion or local failure assignment. It exits through existing core scope mechanics.
limits: Core operation revision/currency bookkeeping and completion still occur on entered refusal; do not assert process-domain metadata is unchanged.
If completion fails, poison/local failure handling can change health and exceptions independently; no healthy failure-control claim survives that condition.
A source-backed early refusal is not, by itself, the requested independent runtime before/after installed-identity witness.
Special shared bootstrap installed-state refusal precedes handle validation and must be tested/classified separately.

signatures: OwnedWorldBackend.call(operation: Callable[[Any, WorldRandomSources], Any], *, lineage: RNGOperation | None) -> Any
OwnedWorldBackend.snapshot(*, lineage: RNGOperation | None) -> dict[str, Any]
OwnedWorldBackend.snapshot_with_capture(capture: Callable[[Any], Any], *, lineage: RNGOperation | None) -> tuple[dict[str, Any], Any]
effects: Successful managed call, snapshot and snapshot_with_capture all increment owner revision (W1013,1030,1058), even when the callback is read-only and consumes no RNG.

A read-only capture callback can return only scalar identity metadata for the actual live provider/Parameters/gradients/storage without returning or retaining those live objects; this is an available managed observation seam, not a revision-neutral one.
Returned tensors are owned copies and cannot serve as live storage-identity witnesses.
Observation between preparation and first install stales the owner's destination revision; reusing ancestor lineage does not waive that check.
Failed-entry/noncallable cases outside guarded regions have the narrower effects recorded in the diagnostic clarification; do not generalize successful revision advancement to every refused call.
